scores.evidence: Exactly one writable primary database at all times. Copying is one-way from that primary (the system of record). Never two databases accepting writes.
scores.rationale: Mechanisms (engine-native replication role switch, fencing, netem latency injection, HL7 SIU async) are correct; minor imprecision such as treating a write pause as 'no downtime' and the sync-vs-async lag claim for zero RPO is acknowledged as assumption.

scores.evidence: Move the app servers unchanged onto cloud VMs. Move the database to a managed service running the same engine. No refactoring.
scores.rationale: Solves the real problem with staged tiers, interprets 'no downtime' explicitly, and states inherited constraints and deferrals with reasons.

scores.evidence: On-prem is the system of record until Phase 4. After the switch, the cloud is the system of record, with copying back to on-prem as a warm fallback
scores.rationale: Single-writer, ownership, fallback and fencing are applied consistently across decisions, phases, validation and cross-cutting tables.

scores.evidence: ≥ 2 full rehearsals on a production-sized copy under replayed peak write load, including failback and the fencing test
scores.rationale: Validations V0–V8 tie to specific risks, run early (latency and PHI gates in Phase 1), have checkable thresholds labeled as assumptions, and include post-cutover monitoring, though production ongoing checks are modest.

scores.evidence: ASSUMPTION: "no downtime" read as "no failed bookings". Clinical operations must confirm.
scores.rationale: Assumptions, unknowns and baselines are explicit and labeled, with revisit triggers stating how the design changes if wrong.

scores.evidence: Fence the old primary so it cannot accept writes: set it read-only and revoke the app's write access. Verify a write attempt is rejected.
scores.rationale: Split brain, lost transactions, late-discovered dependencies, link/zone loss and partner allow-listing are covered with detection and recovery, but retries/duplicate bookings and adversarial input are thin.

scores.evidence: Cutover dashboard: write pause, errors, HL7 backlog, reconciliation
scores.rationale: Deployment via pipeline, per-wave rollback, meaningful signals, named approvers and hypercare are covered; incident ownership and on-call roles are less explicit.

scores.evidence: Cloud running cost and dual-running cost | UNKNOWN: finance supplies the budget before Phase 2
scores.rationale: Dual-running cost limits, reserved-capacity timing and build-vs-buy are noted, but there are no estimates or ranges and few cost drivers (egress, circuits, licensing) are analyzed.

scores.evidence: The point of no return is decommissioning, not this switch.
scores.rationale: Reversibility is classified per decision with revisit triggers, fallbacks and deferred commitments, and the cutover is explicitly made reversible until V8.

scores.evidence: Monolith vs services, and sync vs async: no re-architecture during the move.
scores.rationale: Lift-and-shift scope is disciplined, though the process scaffolding (dependency kinds, phase 0 slice with nine tiers, V0–V8) is somewhat heavy.

scores.evidence: Order the circuits if not done already (they have the longest lead time).
scores.rationale: Phases are ordered by dependency and lead time, each with exit checks, rollback and fallback if checks fail; a team could start immediately.

checklist.evidence: Private connectivity only, no public endpoints. Encryption keys managed by the hospital. Only BAA-covered services.
HL7 feeds to the EHR, patient-registration (ADT) feed in, billing, patient portal, SMS/phone reminder vendor, health information exchange (HIE), reporting/data-warehouse ETL
daily row-count and key-range hash reconciliation over 14 days, including month-end and template generation
Exactly one writable primary database at all times.
The rehearsed failback (switch roles back to on-prem) stays available until V8.
Two diverse private circuits (ExpressRoute or Direct Connect) plus a site-to-site VPN as backup.
Run a disaster-recovery test in the cloud: backup restore and a zone failover within the RTO.
Active Directory remains the identity source. ... break-glass access logged
2-hour load test at 2× peak on an isolated copy, with a batch job running
the lowest-volume window measured in Phase 1. It must avoid month-end and EHR change freezes.
sanitize media to NIST SP 800-88 and keep the destruction certificate.

traps.evidence: Move users in waves by load-balancer weight: IT, then one low-volume clinic, then groups of clinics, then the call center last.
No real PHI reaches cloud storage, because the change-capture filter passes test IDs only.
Every consumer of the database and app found: HL7 feeds to the EHR, patient-registration (ADT) feed in, billing
Monolith vs services, and sync vs async: no re-architecture during the move.

note: Strong, well-sequenced staged migration with single-writer control, rehearsed failback and explicit assumptions; weakest on cost quantification, break-glass/identity detail and clinical cutover communications.
